subject: build recipe
body:
Corrected re-write under the canonical repo slug (the original was mistakenly written under "douglascrockford/JSON-java", the project's former maintainer org visible in repo history, and was unfindable by notes_read for this run's actual slug "stleary/JSON-java" — a dispatch-prompt gap: the agent was never told the canonical slug and inferred it from content instead).

BuildRecipe, proven via jvm_build_probe against 4f859fdf3b5669894c5ed8a305ee5cd5f1fe2b7a:
- baseImage: maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-8 (bare eclipse-temurin:8-jdk fails MISSING_TOOLCHAIN, no mvn)
- buildTool: maven
- buildCommand: mvn clean compile -D maven.compiler.source=8 -D maven.compiler.target=8 -D maven.test.skip=true -D maven.site.skip=true -D maven.javadoc.skip=true
- testCommand: mvn test -D maven.compiler.source=8 -D maven.compiler.target=8 (jacoco prepare-agent/report goals also verified working when coverage is needed)
- flags: -D maven.compiler.source=8, -D maven.compiler.target=8 (matches pom's declared 1.8 source/target and CI's matrix)
- entryPoints (library, no main()): org.json.JSONObject.<init>(String), org.json.JSONArray.<init>(String), org.json.JSONTokener.<init>(String), org.json.XML.toJSONObject(String)
- CI matrix-builds JDK 8/11/17/21/25 with identical mvn invocations (.github/workflows/pipeline.yml)

subject: commit message and issue-reference idiom
body:
Observed while running recall nets over the 12-month window ending at 4f859fdf3b5669894c5ed8a305ee5cd5f1fe2b7a. Hints for adjudication — verify per commit, do not repeat as fact.

Issue references take several shapes, so an adjudicator looking only for "#NNNN" will under-link:
- "#1071: narrow tag-name check to XML metachars only" — leading "#NNNN:" prefix, used by several outside contributors (mechko, OwenSanzas).
- "Fixes #1040, Aligns non-forceList behaviour with forceList" — inline Fixes #NNNN.
- "Fixes CVE-2026-59171" — security fixes may cite a CVE and NO GitHub issue number.
- Branch names carry the issue: merge subjects read "Merge pull request #1067 from mechko/1063-biginteger-exponent-dos", where 1067 is the PR and 1063 is the underlying issue. The PR number and the issue number are DIFFERENT; the branch-name digits are usually the issue.

Workflow shape: maintainer (Sean Leary) merges contributor PRs with merge commits, and the contributor's individual commits are preserved rather than squashed. So a single logical fix is often 2-4 consecutive commits — an initial fix, then follow-ups answering review or SonarCloud. Example: 1063 spans fce83c91 (the actual bound), e40d933d (comment for java:S108), 703ac34a (API overloads). Adjudicate the commit that changes behaviour, not the cleanup that follows it.

High-frequency NON-fix classes in this repo, likely to dominate NOT_BUG_FIX verdicts: "pre-release-YYYYMMDD ..." release-prep commits by the maintainer; SonarQube/SonarCloud cleanup ("more sonarcube fixes", "sonarqube reliability issues") which use the word "fix" but are static-analysis hygiene, not defect repair; README/docs/badge edits; and repeated "Updating to work with java 1.6" compatibility churn. The word "fix" in a subject is weak evidence here specifically because of the Sonar cleanup stream.

subject: callGraphId cg_9b8884491b1e0f2c evicted
body:
While tracing e2cfb5a64150455bf63ad334da9827e7671c9133 (XML.toString element-injection fix), cg_9b8884491b1e0f2c returned Unknown(NotApplicable)/"evicted to bound memory" on BOTH jvm_callgraph_paths and jvm_trace_path_in. No buildHandle was supplied in the tracer's task either, so jvm_method_at_line/jvm_method_body (which need one) were unusable — do not retry those blind, ask the dispatcher for a buildHandle or a rebuild first.

Workaround used successfully: history_file_at on the SAME commit the trace (tr_671686c00eb14244) ran against, read at the relevant line windows, to see the actual (non-polymorphic) call edges by eye, intersected with jvm_trace_executed(traceId) to confirm every node in the chain was actually hit. For org.json.XML this worked cleanly because the chain is entirely static-method-to-static-method with no interfaces/reflection: toString(Object,String) -> toString(Object,String,XMLParserConfiguration) -> private toString(Object,String,XMLParserConfiguration,int,int) [recursive worker, fault site for issue #1071 / CWE-91].

If you hit the same eviction, tell the dispatching agent so cg_9b8884491b1e0f2c (or a fresh graph) gets rebuilt via jvm_callgraph_build — this note is a fallback for when a graph rebuild is not available in-run, not a substitute for one.

subject: callGraphId eviction during path tracing (XML.java / cg_5c26db425148714b)
body: cg_5c26db425148714b (CHA, rooted at XML#escape(String)) served exactly ONE successful call-graph query (jvm_callgraph_chains_to target=XML$1$1#next) before being evicted to bound memory. Every subsequent call against the same id — jvm_callgraph_paths, jvm_callgraph_callers, jvm_trace_path_in — returned Unknown(NotApplicable) with detail "evicted to bound memory — rebuild it with jvm_callgraph_build". path-tracer's toolset does NOT include jvm_callgraph_build, so recovery is not possible from within this agent; the launcher must rebuild and hand back a fresh id if more than one query is needed against a given call graph. Practical consequence: front-load the single highest-value query (usually jvm_callgraph_chains_to on the fault method, which both proves connectivity AND names the entry point in one shot) rather than planning a paths-then-callers-then-trace_path_in sequence against one callGraphId — later calls in that sequence are likely to find the graph already gone.

subject: cg_122c7cd1840643be evicted / no buildHandle for CVE-2026-59171 trace
body:
While tracing fce83c91 (CVE-2026-59171, JSONObject#optBigInteger unbounded BigDecimal.toBigInteger() DoS): callGraphId cg_122c7cd1840643be given in the dispatch prompt was already evicted ("evicted to bound memory — rebuild it with jvm_callgraph_build"). jvm_callgraph_paths, jvm_callgraph_callers and jvm_trace_path_in all returned NotApplicable against it. This agent's toolset does not include jvm_callgraph_build, so rebuild was not possible from within a path-tracer run — the dispatcher needs to rebuild it before the next trace over this call graph id, or hand path-tracer the build tool.

Separately, no buildHandle was supplied in the dispatch prompt, so jvm_method_at_line / jvm_method_body could not be called at all (build_0000000000000000 probe confirmed: NotApplicable "no build registered"). Worked around both gaps by using history_file_at directly on the parent sha to read the method bodies around the diff's old-side line ranges — this resolves method identity/line-to-method mapping just as well when the file is small enough to read in one slice, and cross-validated the resulting call edge (optBigInteger -> objectToBigInteger, single unconditional call) against jvm_trace_executed. For JDK-internal frames (java.math.BigDecimal/BigInteger) no source is available in-repo and no call-graph existed for them either way, so that segment could only be corroborated by trace co-membership, not a graph edge — recorded as a gap in the finding, not asserted as a path.

If dispatching another path-tracer against this same bug/call graph id, rebuild cg_122c7cd1840643be and supply a live buildHandle up front to avoid repeating this.

subject: callGraphId cg_9b8884491b1e0f2c evicted
body:
RESOLVED: cg_9b8884491b1e0f2c was rebuilt by the coordinator mid-run (same content-addressed id) with toJSONObject and toString(Object,String) as entry points over the correct parent build, and is now resident. jvm_callgraph_paths and jvm_trace_path_in both work again and CONFIRM the source-reading workaround described in the superseded version of this note: for org.json.XML#toString(Object,String) -> XML fault site, there is exactly one static path (searchExhausted=true) and jvm_trace_path_in against tr_671686c00eb14244 reports allHopsExecuted=true, missingHops=[].

Takeaway for future tracers: if you see NotApplicable/evicted on a callGraphId, it is worth flagging to the dispatcher and retrying later in the same run rather than treating it as permanent — it was fixed here without a new id being issued. The source-read+trace-intersection workaround is a reasonable stopgap while waiting, and in this case matched the formal graph result exactly, but should still be replaced with the real graph query once available rather than left standing alone.

subject: jvm_harness_run harness contract
body: jvm_harness_run does NOT invoke a main(String[]) method. The generated Runner.java calls `Harness.run()` and expects it to return Object. Harness class must be named exactly "Harness" (public class Harness) with signature `public static Object run() throws Exception`. A harness with only main() fails to compile against BOTH revisions with "cannot find symbol: method run()". This is a compile-error fix, not a reasoning iteration, but worth knowing up front to save a round trip.

subject: path-tracer toolset lacks graph_upsert_bug
body: Task briefs for path-tracer on this repo have asked to persist via "findings_record and graph_upsert_bug", but the path-tracer agent's exposed MCP tool list (as served) contains only findings_record among persistence tools — no graph_upsert_bug schema is granted. Confirmed on run_71e86d4ef19eeb85 while tracing 995fb840f79bf8b9230a08e45cd2289fb21b3cc6. Persisted the PATH finding via findings_record only; if graph writes are actually required, either grant graph_upsert_bug to path-tracer in schemas/tools + agent frontmatter, or have the orchestrating agent perform the graph write itself from the findings_record output.

subject: CHA call graph excludes test-source call sites
body:
cg_3c0ee92a895a1ae3 (entry points JSONObject.stringToValue(String), JSONObject.<init>(String), JSONArray.<init>(String), built from build_4d585be3f2a585ec) does NOT include org.json.junit.* test classes as nodes. jvm_trace_path_in from org.json.junit.JSONObjectTest#testMaxNumberLength()V to JSONObject.<init>(String) returns Unknown(NotApplicable) "cannot resolve ...", and jvm_callgraph_callers on JSONObject.<init>(String) returns zero callers even though it is executed immediately after the test method in tr_09d2aa0f9947e236 (jvm_trace_executed lists both). This graph appears to be built over main sources only (library entry points seeded directly rather than discovered from a test-invoking root), so the segment from a JUnit test method down to the first library entry point can never be OBSERVED via jvm_trace_path_in against this callGraphId - it will always report NotApplicable, not a real disconnect. Future tracers on this repo/build should start their path at the library entry point itself (e.g. JSONObject.<init>(String)) and record the test→entry-point hop as a gap rather than retrying callgraph queries against it.

For this run's bug (testMaxNumberLength / stringToValue unbounded BigInteger), the OBSERVED path from JSONObject.<init>(String) through JSONObject.<init>(String,JSONParserConfiguration) -> JSONObject.<init>(JSONTokener,JSONParserConfiguration) -> parseJSONObject -> JSONTokener.nextSimpleValue(char) -> JSONObject.stringToValue(String) -> JSONObject.stringToNumber(String) was confirmed in two jvm_trace_path_in calls (allHopsExecuted=true both times) before any eviction occurred - unlike other notes on this run, this callGraphId survived 4 queries without eviction.
